decisions.mark: explains that each axis is cleared by a DIFFERENT action — a rebuild for data, a client restart for code — which is why one flag would not have been enough
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `code` | process fingerprint ≠ source fingerprint | Restart the MCP client. A rebuild cannot fix this. ... `data` | `source_changed_files > 0` | `index(action='refresh')` | WHY: The answer gives different remedies per axis (refresh for data, restart for code) but never states that this is why a single flag would not have been enough. || QUOTE: Restart the MCP client. A rebuild cannot fix this. | WHY: The answer gives different remedies per axis (refresh for data, restart for code), but never says that this difference is why a single flag would not have been enough.

decisions.mark: identifies that the schema axis can be UNRESOLVABLE — when the index is newer than the server, no rebuild clears it, because rebuilding re-stamps the same newer version
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "If the index is newer, restart the client, because a rebuild re-stamps the same version." and "On `schema` (server older than index): restart the MCP client. Rebuilding does not clear it." | WHY: The answer says that when the index is newer than the server, a rebuild cannot clear the schema axis because it re-stamps the same version. || QUOTE: If the index is newer, restart the client, because a rebuild re-stamps the same version. | WHY: The answer says that a schema-axis mismatch where the index is newer than the server is not cleared by a rebuild, because the rebuild re-stamps the same version. Step 3 repeats this: "Rebuilding does not clear it." || QUOTE: "If the index is newer, restart the client, because a rebuild re-stamps the same version." | WHY: The answer says that when the index is newer than the server, a rebuild cannot clear the schema axis because it re-stamps the same version.

decisions.mark: states the read/write asymmetry on the code axis: READS stay current because query tools open the database per call, while a BUILD through a stale process writes old pipeline logic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The server refuses to auto-refresh when `matches_source` is false, because an old process rebuilding would re-stamp the index with stale pipeline logic. | WHY: The answer states that writes are refused for stale code, but never says reads stay current because the query tools open the database per call, so the read/write asymmetry is absent. || QUOTE: The server refuses to auto-refresh when `matches_source` is false, because an old process rebuilding would re-stamp the index with stale pipeline logic. | WHY: The answer states that a stale process's build writes old logic, but never says reads stay current because query tools open the database per call, so the read/write asymmetry is absent. || QUOTE: The server refuses to auto-refresh when `matches_source` is false, because an old process rebuilding would re-stamp the index with stale pipeline logic. | WHY: The answer covers the write refusal for stale code, but it never says that reads stay current because query tools open the database per call, so the read/write asymmetry is absent.

decisions.mark: states that the annotation RIDES ON EVERY QUERY REPLY rather than waiting to be asked for, and that it is empty on a current tool
